test_title: PYST 54: SSC GD Constable - English (Held on: 10th December 2021 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Loaded words

options.text: Words that have been used by well-known writers
Words that common people cannot understand
Words that carry more significance than their literal meaning
Words or language that is impolite and rude

solution:
The correct answer is **Words that carry more significance than their literal meaning.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loaded words **mean a word that has more emotional weight or significance than their literal meaning, whether positive or negative.

 
 
• **Example: ***If you want to be the head boy of the school, you should always avoid using loaded words that can offend someone unintentionally. *
 
 
 
• ​Among all the other options, only **Words that carry more significance than their literal meaning** mean** loaded words.**

Therefore, Words that carry more significance than their literal meaning is the correct option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some other idioms and their meanings-
 
• **He has bigger fish to fry- **He has more important matters to attend to than what we are discussing right now.
 
• **Hit the nail on the head- **Get it right the first time.
 
• **He's a chip off the old block- **The son is similar to the father.
